title: Earn up to $1,000 to Invest When You Transfer Your Portfolio to Betashares Direct ($100k Transfer for $1k to Invest)
body:
Deal: Earn up to $1,000 to Invest When You Transfer Your Portfolio to Betashares Direct ($100k Transfer for $1k to Invest)

[AT420] So am I able to transfer my entire Stake portfolio into betashares, wait 12 months, and only pay a $9.50 transfer fee out back to stake? Or am I understanding wrong
[Daniel Plainview] Yes, how else would you interpret the offer? Is pretty straight forward with the core part of the promo.
The OP is not accurate though as the transfer out fees are up to $AUD9.50 per security e.g 10 holdings in your portfolio is a $95 fee.
Its not a bad promo - 1% bump is nothing to sneer at but it does pale to some of the recent ones that Webull did, which although they were only up to 3% bonus - allowed a total of $AUD100,000 to be earnt - and I literally know a person who got this (used their SMSF).
[AT420] Apologies, new to investing so just double checking to make sure I am not missing any details. Thanks for your response Daniel
[Daniel Plainview] No offence meant. :-)
FWIW never trust strangers to properly interpret T&Cs on deals etc - always read them yourself and then compare back to 'the herd' to see if you've missed anything.
[AustriaBargain] What are they doing with it in those 12 months, are they somehow borrowing against it?
[onceupon8] The transfer process mentions "A list of securities you wish to transfer from your Stake (FinClear) account"…..does this mean, I could just transfer one or two of my securities from Stake and be eligible? Or do I have to transfer my whole portfolio?
[Daniel Plainview] Sure but a broker being CHESS sponsored is not a deal breaker in and of itself (IMHO). Betashares at face value is a pretty well regarded and successful operation, I'd find it very unlikely given their market status in Au as the 2nd largest provider of ETF products that they'd go bust and to such an extent that clients investments would not be covered.
Custodian model brokerages (as Beta is) is very common if not the norm in most of the world and seems well implemented in Australia, so I would not let that get between this and using them if you feel it's of use to you.
[Aureus] Your investments are kept in a trust and you retain ownership, so even if they went broke it wouldn't be a huge deal
[Daniel Plainview] Exactly.
Chess is a tad safer with some pretty unlikely stuff e.g broker fraud - but the custodian model is used all over the world as it's pretty darn good.
I mean I can never recall a brokerage in Australia going bust where clients ended up losing $$$ as they were a custodian model - I do recall some banks, but not brokerages. So one is very good (custodian), the other is excellent (chess).
[Daniel Plainview] @suti1: Fair point - but as stated I didn't recall this off the top of my head and not sure how many would without a search - I never said it had never or could never happen.
Suffice to say these are the things folks need to factor in - but I'd personally look at Beta with their fund management market position etc are very different to Opes Prime, who seems to have been a pretty niche operation. Anyway caveat emptor and I'm not an investor with Beta Direct.. :-)
[Aureus] @suti1: Irrelevant.
Opes prime was not a custodial arrangement, if it was the investors would have been safe.
Betashares does not own your shares, it is kept in a separate trust that you maintain ownership of.
With Opes Prime people transferred full ownership of shares to them.
[rheags] Betashares is very unlikely to go broke, but going for a smaller non-chess broker has dangers.
See BBY, it went under in 2015 and it took some people 4+ years to get their shares.
In a custodial model if the broker goes under the liquidator has to sort through the books to work out who owns what, until they have completed this reconciliation you can't get at/transfer your shares.
In the CHESS model, your shares are linked to your HIN maintained by the ASX, so if your broker goes under you just contact another broker and you can do a HIN transfer and have your shares in a day or 2.
Generally custodial is fine, but just need to be aware there are some risks associated with it.
[Aureus] @rheags: ^ That is the real concern. It may take time for your shares to be transferred, but shouldn't take anywhere near 4 years.
I am not across BBY, but it seems like the huge delay was caused by them improperly commingling funds with the trust and inhouse accounts. That caused a huge amount forensic accounting to work everything out.
I don't see how this could happen with Betashares, but yes you do have to trust the company is doing what is legally required of them to do and that is a small additional risk.
[mungicide] How do you find custodian model when it comes to tax time? Do you still get AMMA statement for individual ETF or are they all rolled up to one?
[DingoBilly] Not as good as the Webull bonuses but decent.
[Merlict] The Webull ones were insane, must have cost them a bomb
[Daniel Plainview] Hilariously go back and check the threads here on them - the number of folks who were outright calling them scams and that your money would be stolen etc. There was even one user saying it was a front for the Chinese Govt who would steal your $$$….
Oddly they've not been heard from for some time now. Funny that.
[ihbh] Your comment is call survivor bias. If you were really scammed because you went with higher risk, then what?
[Daniel Plainview] @ihbh: No my guy, my comment is called I read the T&C and knew that a chess sponsored investment was rock solid - other clowns were Henny Pennying it when they had no idea. Anyway I ended up with a very significant sum in total from the bonus and so they look a tad silly.
Survivor bias is nothing like that.

[Asti] As someone who took advantage of it too I can confirm it's real. I got my first payment months ago and it's a was insane amount of money for a promo. I got in a bit early , 2% instead of 3%… but hey can't be too picky for getting a years worth of wages for doing barely anything

I never bothered to transfer my previous holdings from selfwealth, but have already been using BD for current and future purchases.
[BigDog8000] Yep, it looks like it's for existing customers too. To participate just make sure you've enrolled first
[donotuse] It's not Chess-Sponsored, if that's something important to you.
Webull occasionally give 2% bonus up to much higher limit and lower holding period, and they're Chess-Sponsored.
[Daniel Plainview] With respect it's simply untrue that Webull Australia "…occassionally give 2% bonus"!
That was at face value a one time thing done just after they came into Australia to build a book of customers at a massive cost - where they ran consecutive promos which paid a 1%, then 2% then 3% bonus promos. They have not run anything like these for 10mths now. Instead only offering pretty unattractive fractional share promos and QFF points on trades. So they HAVE done it, but this does not in any way indicate a pattern or an ongoing repeat is likely. Very different things.
You're also incorrect that they (Webull) do not have lower holding periods - all their deposit or transfer bonus promos had a minimum of 12mths essentially with the 3% one needing 24mths. Yes, technically you could take funds out IF you put them back in by a certain date but thats kind of semantics.
There is absolutely NO evidence or pattern to indicate that Webull Australia will ever offer such promos again and given what they'd have cost them I would find it from a cost standpoint incredibly unlikely.
[JJo] Last december deal was 3% for webull. At that point they'd been in Australia for quite a while and had been doing deals for a long time. You're right though that it's been a while since they've done a big deal
Note: checked my reward history, 3% deal was until Jan 15
[Daniel Plainview] The deals ran one after the other - so yes they had been here for a while, but this was clearly done to get a market share upgrade rather than an ongoing annual deposit bonus promo.
They'd done promos but nothing like those - and they also had very lucrative referral promos at the same time.
I'd be very happy to be wrong but they look like essentially a one off event - anyway we can all hope.
[Merlict] They've done more than one round of it in other markets, but no I wouldn't hold my breath for a repeat.
[Autonomic] They had ~4% back in apple shares in 2023. The 2%/3% match was well after they entered the AU market.
[Daniel Plainview] I was one of the 'I can't wait for a better deal!' folks who jumped on the Webull 1% promo (thus losing out on their chance to get in on the subsequent 2 and 3% ones - so I would say it's definitely a good deal for folks who can meet the terms of the promo to jump on this Beta one.
I would not expect them to up it to higher levels, the fact they've limited it to $1000 total bonus - shows that they're not deep pocketed like Webull were.
Amusingly there were also a lot of folks who held off investing with Webull feeling that even better offers would come and they never have, nor look likely so sometimes as they say don't look that gift horse in the mouth i.e just take the pretty good deal!
[Dyl] What’s the steps for transferring to them? I have betashare ETFs with CommSec
An extra 1% for free sounds pretty neat, but I assume you’re locked to Betashare ETFs with your money if you sell to move portfolio around? Or do they brokerage any ASX shares (including buys)?
[squeeze] Just be careful I think commsec charge for the transfer because betashares isn't chess. Someone pls confirm..
[Dyl] I’ll look into that
I’ve been looking at moving anyway because the commsec fees come back soon. May only be 0.2% but it’s still a fee, plus they do dump sales for the lower end of the spread instead of closer to even so you lose a couple of decimals there too.
[tajid] Is it possible to only transfer partial portfolio?
[onceupon8] I have the same question. It looks like it is, but it would be good if someone who has done it can comment.
[spaceflight] Just like it's possible to sell only part of your portfolio
[Daniel Plainview] Yes, all brokers allow and actually REQUIRE you to specify the exact holdings that you require transferred over. i.e codes and the numbers of them to go - so you would also be able to specify part of a single holding e.g if you held 1000 DHHF, you could transfer only 500 of them by stating this.
But most common is just to say your entire holdings but you still generally have to state exactly what this will be and provide a position/account statement or similar from your existing broker. Is very simple and generally takes a few business days.
[spaceflight] Offer ends 1 October 2026
Plenty of time to transfer out of Betashares and then back in to maximise the offer.
